metadata.case_name: SHUM TING YUK v. LAM KAM LUEN AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: cashier in a bowling centre and freelance beautician
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: part-time work with relatively few demands

injuries.description: Penetrating injury to the skull allowing air to enter the cranial cavity with loss of consciousness and post-traumatic amnesia.
source: (a) loss of consciousness and a penetrating injury to the skull allowing air to enter the cranial cavity, although no fracture could be detected on X-rays;

The injuries to the mouth noted by the consultant oral surgeon at Princess Margaret Hospital on the day of the accident were loss of a number of teeth, derangement of the occlusion, i.e. inability to close the mouth properly, and a suspected fractured left mandible, although this was never confirmed.
I find that the head injury sustained by the Plaintiff was, as Dr. Choa says, significant, but was not severe, and any damage healed completely within a comparatively short time.
injuries.icd_description: Concussion with incomplete loss of consciousness with amnesia

injuries.description: Lacerations and bruising to the face with consequential scarring; laceration to the right hand.
source: (b) lacerations and bruising to the face and a laceration to the right hand ;

As to the facial scarring, the initial injuries noted at Princess Margaret Hospital were a 5 cm. laceration across the right zygomatic region, a 2 cm. laceration above the nasal bridge, and a 1 cm. laceration over the submental region communicating with the oral cavity, although Dr. Otto Au, who was consulted by the Plaintiff in relation to the scarring in April 1987, noted a total of five scars on the face.

Dr. Au carried out a total of six operations for scar revisions, scar excision and dermabrasion between April 1987 and September 1988 and, in a report of 16th July 1991 noted that the scars had all healed well and were practically invisible, except for that on the right cheek which was still slightly visible.

injuries.description: Extensive damage to the mouth resulting in the loss of six teeth and loss of some supporting alveolar bone, requiring prolonged reconstructive dental surgery including bone graft and implants.
source: (c) extensive damage to the mouth resulting in the loss of six teeth and some of the supporting bone, requiring prolonged dental surgery;

A more detailed report by Professor Robert Clark of the Prince Philip Dental Hospital following examinations on the 12th and 25th November 1987 noted in addition severe loss of alveolar bone, and bone supporting the teeth in the lower law, and recommended extensive restorative treatment.

During this time dental implants were inserted in the bone of the jaw and implant-retained dentures fitted, in addition to numerous other procedures to correct the damage to her teeth, including root canal therapy, amalgam restorations, a ceramo-metal crown and partial upper and lower dentures.

injuries.description: Prolapsed intervertebral disc at L-4/L-5 level with surgical excision and continuing chronic low back pain and some permanent disability.
source: (d) prolapsed intervertebral disc at L-4/L-5 level.
It is not disputed that the Plaintiff suffered an injury to her back for which she was treated by surgical excision of the disc at L4/L5 level in October 1988.

It is clear from this that the Plaintiff did suffer an injury to her back in the accident which has caused continuing pain and discomfort, for which surgery was not a complete answer, and which has resulted in a disability which is likely to be permanent.
injuries.icd_description: Certain specified injuries of abdomen, lower back or pelvis

manifestations.description: Post-traumatic amnesia (period assumed to be in the region of 24 hours)
Derangement of the occlusion, i.e. inability to close the mouth properly
Loss of a number of teeth (six teeth) and severe loss of alveolar bone
Facial scarring (practically invisible except slightly visible scar on right cheek; concealed by sticking plaster)
Sitting tolerance of about one hour
Lumbar-sacral tenderness, full straight leg raising, mild decrease in flexion
Severe depression with loss of self-confidence, fear of going out and inability to work (totally unemployable until treated)

treatments_received: admission to Princess Margaret Hospital and transfer to Queen Elizabeth Hospital (discharged 24 February 1987)
six operations for scar revisions, scar excision and dermabrasion between April 1987 and September 1988
surgical excision of the disc at L4/L5 (October 1988)
extensive restorative dental treatment (root canal therapy, amalgam restorations, ceramo-metal crown, partial dentures, dental implants and implant-retained dentures)
bone graft from right hip (inpatient at Tsan Yuk Hospital from 17 January 1990 to 25 January 1990)
treatments_future: intensive psychiatric treatment and psychotherapeutic counselling (assessed at 6 to 12 months by Dr. Bernard Lau)
replacement dental bridges (allowed replacement twice at cost awarded)

losses.description: Facial scarring, including a slightly visible scar on the right cheek which the Plaintiff conceals with a flesh coloured sticking plaster.
Extensive damage to the mouth with loss of six teeth and supporting bone requiring prolonged reconstructive dental surgery.
Chronic low back pain with reduced lumbar flexion and sitting tolerance of about one hour.
Prevented from permanent employment since the accident and presently totally unemployable until depression is successfully treated.
Change in life and loss of self-esteem and confidence affecting social and occupational prospects as a result of injuries and depression.
Severe depression with loss of self-confidence, fear of going out and inability to work (totally unemployable until treated)
